subject: Renewal uplift: midterm top-up, invoice split & billing lock
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal uplift: midterm top-up, invoice split & billing lock

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, HelixHealth is looking to accelerate the midterm top-up (additional reserved capacity) to cover a Q3 pilot. To make procurement and accounting happy, you asked for: an invoice split option and a billing lock (no mid-invoice adjustments after PO is issued).

I attached a short pricing summary with two practical options:
- Option A: One-time top-up invoiced up front, 60% discount on incremental units for the first quarter (simpler PO).
- Option B: Phased invoicing (50/50 split over 60 days) with 40% discount on incremental units and a monthly amortization schedule on your ledger.

Both options can be added as an amendment to your existing contract; legal noted that a billing-lock clause is straightforward but we need a PO by June 30 to hit the onboarding window.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred invoicing option (A or B) and internal PO timeline.
2) If you need larger than 40% discount on incremental units, I’ll loop in Ben for approval.
3) I’ll push an amendment draft to Legal and share a DocSend once agreed.

Attaching: hlx_pricing_summary.pdf — short table + sample invoice split.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | (415) 555-0183

From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@helixhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixhealth.com, Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift: midterm top-up, invoice split & billing lock

Kimberly —

Thanks for the options and the summary. A few clarifying items from procurement and finance:
- Procurement prefers Option B (phased invoicing) but needs the second invoice to be no later than 60 days from the first.
- Finance needs us to amortize the top-up over 3 months in their ledger (not 12).
- Legal flagged a concern about the billing-lock: they want a clear change-control process so we can’t retroactively change scope without a signed amendment.

Two asks from our side: can you (1) confirm the amortization math for Option B (I’ll attach a sample ledger if useful), and (2) indicate the maximum discount you can approve on the incremental units without an exec sign-off?

If we can get those answers this week we can issue a PO by 6/29.

Best,
Emma
Emma Lewis
Head of Platform Ops, HelixHealth
emma.lewis@helixhealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@helixhealth.com>, procurement@helixhealth.com
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift: midterm top-up, invoice split & billing lock

Emma —

Thanks — quick answers inline:
1) Amortization: Option B amortized over 3 months is fine. I ran the numbers in the attached summary. We can label the invoices as "Deposit" and "Final top-up" with a payment window of 30 days each so that your ledger shows the 3-month allocation.

2) Discount authority: I can offer up to 40% on incremental units from my quota-approved range. Anything above 40% requires manager approval (Ben).

Ben / Jordan — can you confirm if we have flexibility for a one-off 45% discount for Helix (they're a strategic pilot) or if 40% is the hard cap? If we need legal language for a change-control/billing-lock flow, I can draft the amendment and share.

I’ve attached the pricing summary again and a sample invoice layout.

Attachment: hlx_pricing_summary.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal uplift: midterm top-up, invoice split & billing lock

Kim —

45% is a stretch for a midterm top-up unless we see a clear expansion path with a commit uplift in the next 90 days. Irene, do we have margin flexibility to support 45% for a Q3 pilot if Helix commits to a forecasted +50% capacity increase by year-end?

If not, 40% is the ask-to-approve sweet spot. Jordan — if we go 40% and structure as phased (50/50) with a billing-lock and PO by 6/29, operations can prioritize onboarding.

Irene — can you confirm a quick margin calc? We need to respond to customer by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Ben
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@helixhealth.com>, procurement@helixhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal uplift: midterm top-up, invoice split & billing lock

Emma —

Quick update per internal: we can confirm Option B (phased invoicing) with amortization over 3 months and a billing-lock that requires a signed amendment for scope changes. Discount: we can commit to 40% on incremental units without further approvals.

If Helix is willing to provide a forecasted commit (not a hard obligation) that shows a likely +50% capacity increase by EOY, we can escalate a one-time promotional 45% to the leadership team for approval — but that will require a short exec review and a DocuSign addendum.

I attached an amendment draft with the billing-lock language and the invoice layout (amendment-draft-2026-06-18.docx). If this works, please: (1) confirm Option B, (2) confirm PO issuance by 6/29, and (3) if you want us to pursue the 45% promo, say so and we’ll open the exec review.

Attachment: amendment-draft-2026-06-18.docx

Look forward to your note — happy to jump on a 15-min call if helpful.

Best,
Kimberly
